# Panoramax outside the catalog: where is the 360° imagery we do not track yet?

**Ran:** 2026-10-01 ·
**Record:** [`panoramax-world-screen_metrics.json`](panoramax-world-screen_metrics.json) and [`panoramax-world-screen_clusters.csv`](panoramax-world-screen_clusters.csv) ·
**Generated by:** `python scripts/panoramax_world_screen_analyze.py --docs-dir docs/experiments` ·
**Collected by:** `scripts/panoramax_world_screen_collect.py --execute` (see Provenance) ·
**Issue:** [#406](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/406).
Instrument: the [#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) growth screen, documented in [`panoramax-feasibility.md`](panoramax-feasibility.md).

## Verdict

**The untracked 360° imagery on Panoramax is overwhelmingly French municipal and metropolitan programmes, and they dwarf everything the catalog holds.**
The screen found 516 clusters of places with at least 2,000 360° pictures within 10 km; 456 of them are not within 25 km of any catalog city, and 322 clear the candidate threshold.
148 of those 322 candidates are in France, 45 in Germany, 24 in Belgium, and 17 in the United States and Canada.
The richest untracked cluster (Strasbourg, 3,550,600 360° pictures) holds more than six times the richest tracked one (Des Moines, 565,529).

**The US candidates are an order of magnitude smaller, and where probed they are single volunteer drives, not programmes.**
The 17 new US clusters have a median bound of 17,413 360° pictures and a maximum of 69,541 (Waterloo, Iowa), against a median of 9,120 and a maximum of 3.55 M over all 456 new clusters.
Nine of the 17 are in Iowa, and the two sampled with a 20-picture `/api/search` (Ottumwa, Norman) were each one day's capture by the research pass's reading of the response.

The decision this supports is a registration shortlist, not a registration: every number here is an **upper bound**, and [#406](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/406)'s acceptance items 2–4 (manifest, geometry checked against the GeoNames point, same-day enrolment, a re-run of the Mapillary probe) come before any city is added.

## The question

On 2026-10-01 the catalog had no untracked Mapillary pool left (0 never-collected, 0 overdue) while nights ran under capacity, so growth means new cities.
Mapillary and Panoramax 360° coverage is what informs future Project Sidewalk deployments.
The question was: **where outside the catalog is there enough recent 360° imagery to be worth registering a city for?**
The Panoramax half could be answered by measurement, cheaply, with an instrument we already trust; the Mapillary half was mostly web research (below).

## Method

### The instrument

The standing #316 screen reads the v2 `grid` layer of `api.panoramax.xyz` at z6: res-6 H3 hexagons (~36 km² each) carrying `nb_pictures`, `nb_360_pictures`, `nb_flat_pictures` and `date`, the newest capture in the hexagon.
`panoramax_screen.hexes_from_tile` and `merge_hexes` decode it; this study imports them rather than re-deriving them.
Instead of the catalog's frozen grids, it was pointed at eight regions: CONUS plus southern Canada (84 tiles), Europe −10.5..30.5°E × 35.5..60.5°N (64), Turkey (9), Taiwan (2), Japan (12), south-east Australia (16), the southern cone of South America (36) and Mexico (12) — **235 tiles**.
New Zealand was dropped to stay under a 250-request cap.

### The derivation (offline)

1. A **place** is a GeoNames `cities15000` row.
   Its bound is the sum of `nb_360_pictures` over hexagons whose centre lies within **10 km** of the GeoNames point; places under **2,000** are dropped.
2. Places are clustered greedily in descending bound order: a place within **20 km** of an existing cluster's anchor joins it.
   A cluster reports its **anchor's** bound under the name and point of its most populous member, which is why "Strasbourg" carries the 3,550,600 of its Lingolsheim anchor rather than Strasbourg's own 3,364,687.
3. A cluster is **tracked** when that named point is within **25 km** of any catalog city (the #298 reuse radius), enabled or not.
4. A new cluster is a **candidate** at ≥ 5,000, or ≥ 2,000 in the US and Canada (the deployment priority).

The catalog is a 2026-10-01 production snapshot of 1,232 cities (1,223 enabled), read as a CSV, never the database; its sha256 is in the record.

### Pacing

Sequential, 30/min mean with the #292 shifted-exponential gaps at CV 0.6, from a laptop, stopping on the first 403 or 429.
No rate limit is documented for this host, so that is the collector's own conservative rate, not a probe of the limit.

## Findings

### 1. The traffic: 239 requests, no refusal

| | n | Result |
|---|---|---|
| z6 tiles | 235 | 201 × 200, **34 × 204**, 0 × 404, 0 × 403/429 |
| `/api/search?limit=20` probes | 4 | 4 × 200 (Ottumwa IA, Layton UT, Norman OK, Immokalee FL) |

The tiles ran 16:46:23Z–16:56:51Z (628 s), an effective 22.36/min against the 30/min mean target, because the research script slept its jittered gap after each response, so every response's latency added to the period.
Tile bodies totalled 40,135,025 bytes: p50 26,055, p90 415,788, p95 779,000, max 3,271,689 (n = 235).
Latency p25 0.635 s, p50 0.74 s, p95 1.42 s, max 2.5 s.
Inter-request gaps at the log's one-second resolution: p25 2, p50 2, p75 3, p95 5, max 8 s (n = 234).
Every tile response carried `Server: nginx/1.31.6` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`; none carried a rate-limit or `Retry-After` header.

**Flagged: an empty tile answered 204, not 404.**
`download_panoramax._fetch_tile` (which the screen imports), `panoramax_screen._refuse_if_endpoint_moved` and `docs/census.md` all describe an empty area as "200 with no layer" and a 404 as the empty tile; here, at z6, all 34 empty tiles were **204 No Content** and none was a 404.
Read from the code rather than exercised: a 204 misses the 404 branch, `raise_for_status` does not raise on a 2xx, and unless its Content-Type is an error page the empty body is returned as a tile that decodes to no hexagons.
So it would most likely read as empty — but it is not COUNTED as empty, so the all-empty "moved endpoint" guard cannot see one, and the 204s' Content-Type was not logged.
Whether z15 answers the same was not measured; no requests were spent on it.

### 2. The hexagons: 261,913, and most hold no 360° imagery

The 235 tiles decoded **261,913** distinct hexagons holding 116,562,471 pictures, of which 51,980,094 are 360° (44.6%) and 64,582,377 flat.
Only **74,915** hexagons (28.6%) hold any 360° picture at all.

| Per hexagon (n) | p25 | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all pictures (261,913) | 4 | 17 | 185 | 820 | 1,718.4 | 235,828 |
| 360° pictures (261,913) | 0 | 0 | 26 | 297 | 775 | 234,472 |
| 360° where positive (74,915) | 46 | 150 | 496 | 1,400 | 2,576.3 | 234,472 |

The newest-capture date per hexagon is recent — 72,756 hexagons date to 2025 and 45,089 to 2026 — but **16 carry a date before 2000**, eight of them the year `0026`.
They are counted, not dropped (`n_hex_dates_before_2000`), and they are the same lesson as #213: a provider's capture date is read as served, and a date that cannot be true has to be guarded at every reader.

### 3. Places and clusters

Of 33,976 GeoNames places, **2,180** have a 10 km bound of at least 2,000 360° pictures, and 1,324 of those are not within 25 km of a catalog city.
**The place bounds double-count, and by a lot**: summed over the 2,180 places they come to 180,252,634 360° pictures, **3.47×** the 51,980,094 the screen decoded in total, because neighbouring places draw on the same hexagons (every Lyon arrondissement reports roughly Lyon's bound).
Clustering is what makes the list readable: 516 clusters, a median of 1 place each (p75 3, p90 8, p95 14, max 182 — Paris).

| 360° bound, 10 km (n) | p25 | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| new clusters (456) | 4,240 | 9,120 | 23,335 | 69,876 | 160,897 | 3,550,600 |
| tracked clusters (60) | 5,712 | 12,601 | 49,538 | 139,036 | 322,037 | 565,529 |
| new clusters, US and Canada (17) | 5,731 | 17,413 | 53,011 | 64,291 | 69,355 | 69,541 |

The 360° share of a new cluster's imagery (bound 360° ÷ bound all) is p25 0.348, p50 0.70, p75 0.935 (n = 456): many candidates are flat-heavy, so the 360° bound, not the total, is the number to rank on.

**Immokalee is the one case where the probe contradicts the counter**: the tile `type` says 85.6% 360°, while the 20-picture `/api/search` sample was flat phone imagery.
The probe's per-picture findings (instance, camera, capture day) were read off the response and are recorded in the research summary, not in this record — only the four probes' status, size and latency are (see "What is not traceable").

### 5. Already tracked: the enable and enrol leads

60 clusters fall within 25 km of a catalog city (`tracked` in the record, with the matched `city_id` and distance).
Three of them match a **disabled** catalog city, all Brussels: Brussels itself (120,696), Leuven (66,513, 24.1 km) and Kortenberg (30,955, 13.9 km).
The largest tracked cluster that is plainly NOT the city it matched is **Layton, Utah: 320,065 360° pictures (one hexagon 45,774), newest 2025-09-14, 18.1 km from Ogden's point** — so it counts as "tracked" under the 25 km rule while almost certainly lying outside Ogden's frozen grid.
Waukee (120,369, 21.8 km from Des Moines), Independence and Liberty (Kansas City, 13.8 and 21.8 km) are the same shape at smaller scale.
The 25 km rule is a reuse radius for registration, not a coverage test, and this list is where that difference shows.

### 6. The Mapillary half (web research and a probe that stopped at request 2)

Most of the Mapillary candidates came from web research (Mapillary blog and showcase, CompleteTheMap 2025–2026, camera-grant recaps, OSM diaries), which no code can reproduce; what is recorded is what can be checked (`mapillary` in the record):

- The web table has **62 rows**; recomputing each downtown point's distance to the catalog snapshot puts **23 within 25 km and 39 beyond it**, matching the table's own labels (20 "yes", 3 "near", 39 "no").
- A Graph API probe was planned for **44** points (two calibration towns, then 42 candidates) at 3 s spacing with `limit=2000`.
  **Request 1** (Laurens, Iowa, a 2×2 km box) returned 2,000 panos — the cap, so a floor — every one captured 2025-11-04 by **one creator, `GIS_ISG`**, with no organisation and none on foot.
  **Request 2** (Lansing, Michigan) returned **HTTP 500, code 1, "Please reduce the amount of data you're asking for"** — a payload-size error from `limit=2000` with six fields over a dense box, not the rate-limit error (code 4) and not a block.
  The probe stopped on its first non-200 by design, so **42 planned probes were never sent**, and 60 of the table's 62 rows carry no API check at all.
- **Flagged**: 2,000 is the Graph API's page cap as this repo records it ([`mapillary-user-activity.md`](mapillary-user-activity.md)), yet a request at that cap was refused for size; no response-size ceiling below the page cap is recorded anywhere in this repo.
  A re-run should use `limit` ≤ 200, or fewer fields.

The single creator at Laurens is the most useful Mapillary result, and it is a lead about an uploader rather than a city (it feeds [#383](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/383)); n = 1 box, capped, so it says nothing about that account's other towns.

## What this justifies

- A shortlist to register, led by the French programmes (Strasbourg, Lyon/Villeurbanne, Bordeaux, Lille, Laval, Saint-Nazaire, Caen, Montpellier, Nantes, Brest, Orléans, Bayonne) plus Mannheim, Kortrijk, Ulm, Kilkenny and the US tail — each measured with the screen's `--measure` (z14) on a computed grid **before** it is registered, since geometry is frozen.
- For French métropoles, a **downtown** centre, not a métropole centroid; the GeoNames point is a populated-place point and is the one to check the grid offset against (#298's four bad matches).
- Ogden (or a separate Layton) and Brussels (with Leuven) are enable/enrol decisions, not registrations.
- No pacing change.
  239 requests at 30/min drew no refusal and no rate-limit header, which is consistent with the current rate and says nothing about a faster one.

## Caveats

- **Upper bounds, never coverage.** A res-6 hexagon is ~36 km², larger than most towns, and the 10 km sum overlaps between neighbours (3.47× in aggregate). Rank order is the robust output; an absolute number is not a city count.
- **The hex `date` is the newest capture in the hexagon**, so one fresh sequence makes an old corpus look recent, and 16 hex dates are impossible.
- **The tile `type` is the 360° signal**, and Immokalee is one case where a sample of pictures disagrees with it.
- **Unscreened**: Africa, South and South-East Asia, the Middle East beyond Turkey, Canada north of ~50.5°N, New Zealand, Alaska and Hawaii, and Argentina west of 71°W or south of 41°S. A zero here means "not screened", never "no imagery".
- **"Tracked" means within 25 km of a catalog point**, enabled or not; it is not a claim that the catalog's grid covers the cluster (Layton).
- **The catalog snapshot is a CSV taken on the day**, not a live read; a city registered since then is not reflected.

## What is not traceable to the record

Stated plainly, so nobody quotes these as measurements:

- The **programme evidence** for named candidates (Strasbourg's Eurométropole programme, Villeurbanne's full 360° IGN capture, Lille's contributor rank, Bayonne's municipal helmet-camera programme, Ulm's own instance, Kilkenny's camera grant) is web research recorded in the gitignored research summary, with URLs, not here.
- The **`/api/search` per-picture findings** (Ottumwa and Norman each a single capture day, equirectangular; Immokalee flat phone imagery) come from the probe script's printed output, which was not saved as a file; only the four requests' status, size and latency are in the record.
- **Which tracked cities are already enrolled on Panoramax** is not in the raw data (the snapshot carries `enabled`, not channel membership), so the record cannot split tracked clusters into enrolled and not-enrolled.
- The **44 planned Mapillary probes** is the length of the research probe script's target list, written into the analysis as a constant.
- **Mapillary-only candidates** (Providenciales, Salzburg's on-foot project, Idaho Springs, the camera-grant towns) rest entirely on web evidence; Salzburg also screens 16,673 360° on Panoramax (rank 174), which is the only part of its case that is measured.

## Provenance

The 2026-10-01 pass was collected by research scripts kept beside their raw output in the gitignored `experiments/candidate-360-cities-2026-10-01/` (`panoramax/screen_regions.py` for the tiles, `panoramax/probe_search.py` for the four searches, `mapillary/probe.py` for the Graph API), from a laptop, never a collection host.
`scripts/panoramax_world_screen_collect.py` is the tile collector made reproducible: the same regions, zoom, request order, cap, mean rate and output schema, through `panoramax_feasibility.Fetcher` (whose pacer spaces request starts, so a re-run runs nearer 30/min than this log's 22.4); its plan is pinned by `tests/test_panoramax_world_screen.py` to the 235 tiles and per-region split the log records.
`scripts/panoramax_world_screen_analyze.py` is the committed derivation, and it reproduces the research pass's own `places_ranked.csv` (2,180 rows), `candidates.csv` (322) and `already_tracked.csv` (60) **row for row** on every bound, hexagon count, newest date, catalog match and distance — checked when it was written.
The record stores every input's sha256 and no GeoNames population (it only picks a cluster's name).

## Replicating

```bash
python scripts/panoramax_world_screen_collect.py               # dry run: the 235-tile plan, no request
python scripts/panoramax_world_screen_collect.py --execute     # ~10 min at 30/min; never on a makelab host
python scripts/panoramax_world_screen_analyze.py --docs-dir docs/experiments   # offline
```

The analysis also needs `prod_catalog_cities.csv` (a `city_id, display_name, country_name, enabled, lat, lon` export of the production catalog) and the two Mapillary files under the raw directory; a fresh run of the collector will differ, since the federation grows weekly.
